newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF to negotiate new credit package with Romania.
newsitem.headline: IMF to negotiate new credit package with Romania.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is to negotiate a new memorandum for extending credits to Romania with the new centrist governing coalition, President Emil Constantinescu's office said on Thursday.

The president's office said a team of experts would arrive this weekend and evaluate the state of the economy within a week. Negotiations to replace the current suspended credit arrangement with a new programme would start in the new year.
It said IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus would visit Romania later this month.

Constantinescu, who ousted ex-communist Ion Iliescu in last month's election, has just had talks with the Fund's chief negotiator for Romania, Poul Thomsen. Central Bank chief Mugur Isarescu also attended.
The president's office said the two sides would work out new conditions for resuming credits once indicators outlining the state of the economy had been clearly established.

"We didn't talk about details, we talked about phases," it quoted Constantinescu saying. "The first phase will be that of analysis and the second one of negotiations. Negotiations will come after we have the correct reflection (of the economy)."
He said the legacy left by the ousted leftist government was "very serious and this is how international lenders view it as well".
